title: Control Assertion Composer: automated artifact bundling with provenance chains
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a composable backend service and Console UX that assembles audit-ready control assertions for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 reviewers. The service will automatically gather time-bound artifacts (logs, policy snapshots, access lists, S3 object manifests, retention decisions), produce a tamper-evident provenance chain for each artifact bundle, and expose signed snapshot packages that map to control IDs. This ticket covers the product scope: control mapping model, retention-simulation runner, evidence bundler, and Console API/UX for exporting assertions.
goals: Enable one-click generation of an 'assertion bundle' for specific control(s) and time window
Include provenance metadata (hashes, collection timestamp, collector identity) for each artifact
Support retention policy simulation to show what evidence would have been available under current or historical retention settings
Map output bundles to SOC 2/ISO control IDs and produce a human-readable assertion summary
Provide machine-readable export (signed JSONL + tarball) and Console download links with TTL-signed URLs
non_goals: Full legal attestation — this is tooling to assemble evidence, not to replace auditor judgement
Long-term archival storage of every generated bundle (we will store metadata and a short retention cache only)
acceptance_criteria: Given a time window and a selected set of controls, the system can produce an assertion bundle that includes at least three artifact types (policy snapshot, access log excerpt, retention config) for that window
Every artifact in the bundle contains provenance metadata: collector id, collection timestamp, SHA-256 hash, source URI
Bundles can be downloaded from the Console as a signed package; the signature verifies with internal KMS keys
Retention-simulation mode can be toggled and shows an overlay explaining which artifacts would be missing under shorter retention periods
Control mapping in the bundle must include the authoritative control id, a brief rationale, and links to the original artifact locations
out_of_scope: Building new collectors for every possible system — we will reuse existing evidence collectors and provide an adapter SDK
Replacing existing audit log infrastructure — collectors will read from existing sinks (S3, BigQuery, internal event streams)
solution_overview: Introduce a new microservice 'assertion-composer' that subscribes to evidence collector APIs and an on-demand snapshot endpoint. The composer will accept a control list and a time range, orchestrate lightweight collector queries (with retention-aware filters), compute artifact hashes, and assemble a provenance manifest. A signing step produces a signed bundle using our KMS. Console will add an 'Assertion Builder' flow with preview, retention-simulation toggle, and download endpoint.
architecture_notes: Composer will be written in Go for low latency and predictable memory usage
Collectors expose a unified REST interface: /collect?source=...&from=...&to=...&preview=true
Provenance manifest schema: flat list of artifact entries (source_uri, artifact_type, sha256, collected_at, collector_id, retention_policy_id)
Signing uses KMS asymmetric keys; signature embedded in package manifest and verifiable by auditors using a public certificate
Temporary storage: bundles written to internal object store with TTL=30d; metadata retained in ledger for 365d
data_flow: User requests assertion from Console -> Console calls composer API with controls + time range -> Composer queries adapters for each collector -> Composer validates artifacts, computes hashes and provenance entries -> Composer creates signed bundle and stores package -> Console shows preview and download link (signed, expiring)
ui_changes: New Console page: 'Assertion Builder' under Compliance > Evidence
Controls checklist with mapping view (control id, description, expected artifact types)
Retention-simulation toggle with visual indicators for missing artifacts
Bundle preview modal showing artifact list and provenance metadata, with 'Download Bundle' CTA
api_contracts: POST /v1/composer/compose -> {controls: [ids], from: ISO8601, to: ISO8601, mode: 'live'|'simulate'} returns {bundle_id, preview: {artifact_count, missing_estimate}}
GET /v1/composer/bundles/{id} -> returns signed bundle tarball URL or 404
POST /v1/composer/verify -> {bundle_manifest, signature} returns {valid: true|false, signer: cert_id}
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest generation and hash verification
Integration tests with two existing collectors (s3-manifests adapter, ibm-logs-adapter) using replayed datasets
E2E tests: Console request -> composer -> bundle verification using a test KMS key
Manual audit run with internal compliance team to validate mapping quality
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only, composer queries with sample datasets (2 weeks)
Beta: opt-in for 3 customers on Dedicated/Private with compliance needs (4 weeks)
GA: public release tied to evidence-collector-2026.03 release, with docs and auditor FAQ
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Exposing sensitive artifact content in bundles -> Mitigation: redaction policy and per-bundle access controls; support for exporting only metadata
Risk: Signature key compromise -> Mitigation: enforce KMS key rotation and hardware-backed keys for production
Risk: Large bundle sizes causing timeouts -> Mitigation: limit default artifact types, stream bundle creation, provide async job status
